costGuide.title: Lexus 8AR-FTS Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an 8AR-FTS typically takes 10-14 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent Lexus specialist) - the turbocharger and water‑to‑air intercooler add complexity .
paragraphs: What moves the price most for this engine is whether the replacement unit has been decarbonised (intake valves) and whether the high‑pressure fuel pump and turbocharger are fresh. A reconditioned 8AR-FTS with documented carbon cleaning and a new HPFP is well worth the premium - these are the two key service items on this engine. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for more detail.

failures.title: Lexus 8AR-FTS Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Carbon buildup on intake valves - D-4ST side effect
items.whatHappens: Like many direct‑injection petrol engines, the 8AR-FTS does not have fuel washing over the intake valves. Over time, crankcase vapours and EGR soot bake onto the intake valves, reducing airflow and causing rough idle, hesitation under load, and reduced fuel economy. This is the most common maintenance item on the 8AR-FTS, and while Lexus's D-4ST system includes port injectors that do provide some valve cleaning at certain load points, buildup still occurs-particularly on vehicles used primarily for short trips.
items.repairVsReplace: Walnut‑shell blasting of the intake valves (£400-£800) restores performance. This is a service item, not a failure. A reconditioned engine should include a professionally cleaned intake system.

items.title: High‑pressure fuel pump failure - stalling, long cranking
items.whatHappens: The high‑pressure fuel pump (HPFP) on the 8AR-FTS can develop internal wear, leading to reduced fuel pressure, long crank times, hesitation, and in some cases, stalling. This has been reported on both IS200t and NX200t models, particularly on earlier production units (2015-2017).
items.repairVsReplace: The HPFP is a standalone component costing £500-£1,200 parts and labour. It does not write off the engine-but prompt attention is recommended, as low fuel pressure can cause lean running and potential engine damage over time.

items.title: Water pump and thermostat housing leaks
items.whatHappens: The plastic thermostat housing and water pump on the 8AR-FTS can develop coolant leaks over time. This is a common issue across many modern Toyota/Lexus turbo engines. Symptoms include visible coolant residue, a sweet smell, and-if ignored-overheating.
items.repairVsReplace: Both components are replaceable as standalone items (£400-£800 each). Neither typically writes off the engine-but ignoring a leak can lead to overheating and head gasket damage.

items.title: Turbocharger wastegate rattle (early units)
items.whatHappens: Some early 8AR-FTS engines exhibit a rattle from the turbocharger wastegate actuator, particularly on throttle lift‑off. This is more of an NVH issue than a performance or reliability concern-it does not affect boost delivery or long‑term durability.
items.repairVsReplace: If the rattle is minor, it's generally safe to ignore. If it becomes severe, the wastegate actuator can be replaced (specialist job, £500-£1,000). It rarely requires a full turbo replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: 2018+ 8AR-FTS units appear to have improved HPFP and water pump hardware, with fewer reported failures. Carbon buildup is a maintenance item across all years-regular use of premium fuel and occasional Italian tune‑ups (extended high‑RPM running) can help mitigate buildup.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 8AR-FTS
variants.intro: The 8AR-FTS is Lexus's 2.0‑litre D-4ST turbocharged petrol engine. The code is physically stamped on the engine block-typically on the front side of the block, just below the cylinder head on the driver's side (UK passenger side), or on a machined pad near the bellhousing. Commonly confused with: - 8NR-FTS - the 1.2‑litre turbocharged engine used in the Toyota Auris, Corolla, and C‑HR (1.2T). It shares the same D-4ST technology but is a smaller displacement-completely different engine family, not interchangeable. - 8AR-FTS - (same code, but note that the 8AR family is also used in some Chinese‑market Toyota and Lexus vehicles with different emissions calibration; UK‑market cars use a specific calibration that may differ from JDM or US‑spec engines). - A25A-FTS - the 2.5‑litre Dynamic Force turbo engine (not the hybrid A25A‑FXS) used in some markets-completely different family, not a swap.

relatives.description: the 3.5‑litre V6 that powered earlier IS350 and GS350 models. The 8AR‑FTS replaced the V6 in the IS200t and NX200t, offering similar power with significantly better fuel economy and lower emissions. A very different character - the V6 is smoother and more sonorous, but the turbo four delivers more mid‑range torque.

the 2.4‑litre turbocharged engine introduced in newer Lexus models (NX350, RX350) as the replacement for the 8AR‑FTS. It delivers significantly more power (275-280 hp) and torque (317-317 lb‑ft) with updated fuel injection and a larger turbocharger. The T24A represents Lexus's next‑generation turbo petrol architecture - not a swap option.

the 1.2‑litre turbocharged engine from the same D‑4ST family, used in the Toyota Auris, Corolla, and C‑HR. It shares the same direct‑injection technology but is a completely different displacement - not interchangeable.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 8AR-FTS - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 8AR‑FTS can be a cost‑effective choice for older IS200t/NX200t values, provided the donor has documented service history. The key checks are: (1) has the intake valves been decarbonised? (2) has the high‑pressure fuel pump been replaced? A used unit with a clean carbon history and a recent HPFP offers excellent value-but always budget for preventative carbon cleaning if the history is unclear. Link once: [used engines service]

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A properly reconditioned 8AR‑FTS should include a professional walnut‑shell decarbonisation of the intake valves, a new high‑pressure fuel pump, a new water pump and thermostat housing, fresh spark plugs, and a full top‑end gasket set. The turbocharger should be inspected and rebuilt if necessary. This is the sweet spot for IS200t and NX200t owners-you get a like‑new engine with the two key weaknesses addressed. Reconditioned units typically come with a 12-24 month warranty. Link once: [reconditioned engines service]

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is only justified for low‑mileage, cherished vehicles (e.g. a clean‑car IS200t with low chassis miles). A quality rebuild will include bottom‑end bearings, piston rings, a full timing system refresh, and turbocharger inspection. This is the most expensive option but offers the closest thing to a new engine. Link once: [rebuilt engines service]

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All options above can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Lexus specialists. Each quote includes warranty details and delivery options. Link once: [supply and fit service]
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The 8AR‑FTS sits in vehicles worth £6,000-£16,000 depending on year and mileage (IS200t, NX200t). A reconditioned engine at £2,200-£3,800 represents roughly 25-50% of the car's value-which is a justifiable investment for a premium turbo Lexus that, once refreshed, will outlast the chassis. For a higher‑mileage IS200t worth under £5,000, a used engine with a solid warranty is often the most sensible financial choice. Always factor in the condition of the turbocharger and transmission before committing to an expensive reconditioned engine.

items.answer: A reconditioned 8AR‑FTS typically costs £2,200-£3,800 supply‑only, with fitted prices around £2,900-£4,800. Used units start from £1,500-£2,500, and full rebuilds from £3,500-£5,500. Get an 8AR‑FTS quote now

items.question: What is the most common problem with the 8AR‑FTS?
items.answer: The most frequently reported issues are carbon buildup on intake valves (typically 40,000-80,000 miles) and high‑pressure fuel pump failure (50,000-100,000 miles). Compare prices for an 8AR‑FTS with carbon cleaning and HPFP already addressed
bullets: Water pump leaks are another known maintenance item (£400-£800).
None of these are catastrophic if addressed promptly - the 8AR‑FTS is generally very durable.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 8AR‑FTS?
items.answer: For lower‑value vehicles (e.g. an older IS200t under £5,000), a used engine with a solid warranty is often the most sensible choice, provided the donor has documented service history and ideally a recent carbon clean. For cars worth £6,000+, a reconditioned unit is the sweet spot - it comes with professional decarbonisation, a new high‑pressure fuel pump, fresh water pump, and a 12‑24 month warranty. Rebuilt engines are only recommended for very low‑mileage or cherished examples. Compare used vs reconditioned 8AR‑FTS prices
bullets: Always confirm the replacement unit has addressed carbon buildup and the HPFP.

items.question: How do I know if my Lexus has the 8AR‑FTS?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on the block (typically on the front side, just below the cylinder head on the driver's side) and is also on your V5C under “Engine number”. Alternatively, enter your registration above and we'll confirm your exact fitment. Check your engine via registration
bullets: Don't confuse it with the 8NR‑FTS (1.2‑litre turbo) - they are not interchangeable.
If your IS or NX is badged "200t" with a 2.0‑litre turbo petrol engine, it's almost certainly the 8AR‑FTS.

items.question: How long does an 8AR‑FTS engine typically last?
items.answer: With proper maintenance, the 8AR‑FTS is expected to exceed 200,000 miles. The engine is chain‑driven, so no timing belt replacement is needed. Regular oil changes (every 10,000 miles or 12 months, using the correct 0W‑20) and premium fuel (to minimise carbon buildup) are critical to longevity. The carbon buildup is a service item, not a terminal failure - a walnut‑blast every 60,000-80,000 miles keeps it fresh. The HPFP is a wear item that should be addressed if symptoms appear. With these maintenance items observed, the 8AR‑FTS is a robust and durable turbo petrol.
